chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
"Do not sell a ready-to-be-bred mount for ten foals from the offspring of a pregnant animal from the coming year."

key_terms.رَاحِلَةً: A mount or beast of burden, often implying a breeding female
key_terms.عَاجِلَةً: Ready, immediate, or available (referring to the animal being ready to breed or deliver)
key_terms.قَابِلٍ: Coming, future, or next (referring to the time of delivery)
key_terms.مَلاَقِيحَ: Foals or young animals, plural of malqah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a pregnant animal for its future offspring?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prohibits this specific transaction to prevent *gharar* (uncertainty) regarding the number and viability of the unborn offspring, a key principle in Shia commercial jurisprudence. This ruling is situated within the broader discussion of *bay' al-wahid bi al-ithnayn* (selling one for two or more), illustrating how deferred delivery of livestock offspring introduces risk that invalidates the contract. The hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on clarity and certainty in trade agreements to protect parties from potential dispute.
